paragraphs: Here's what jumps out at me, friend. This whole house is a mess of hurt, and look at what the LORD does. "When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb" (Genesis 29:31). That's the heart of this passage: God sees the one who is unloved.

Now, I have to be honest about the rest of it. Leah keeps hoping a baby will win her husband's love, saying "Surely my husband will love me now" (Genesis 29:32). Rachel and Leah keep trying to win the scoreboard with servants and mandrakes, and I think both of them are carrying a hurt that runs deep. Then something shifts in Leah, and with her fourth son she says, "This time I will praise the LORD" (Genesis 29:35).

So take this with you, baker. When you feel overlooked, or you catch yourself chasing somebody's approval, the One who sees you is already looking. And watch this: God stays faithful even while people are scrambling. He listens to Leah (Genesis 30:17), and He remembers Rachel (Genesis 30:22). Jacob's story isn't over, and neither is yours.
